digest: Malicious PowerShell execution originating from winword.exe on FIN-DB-02 attempted to download and execute a payload from 203.0.113.77, followed by persistent C2 communication. Initial claims of routine maintenance are false.

evidence_findings.title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution
evidence_findings.subject: powershell.exe on FIN-DB-02
evidence_findings.evidence: The process 'winword.exe' spawned 'powershell.exe' on host 'FIN-DB-02' with a hidden, base64-encoded command. The decoded command 'IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient)' indicates an attempt to download and execute remote content.
evidence_findings.conclusion: This is highly suspicious behavior, often indicative of a malicious document exploit or initial access vector.

evidence_findings.title: Unauthorized External Communication
evidence_findings.evidence: The PowerShell command attempted to download a file from 'hxxps://203.0.113.77/update.dat'. Subsequently, outbound network connections from '10.20.8.42' to '203.0.113.77' on port 443 were observed immediately after PowerShell execution, with 120 connections over 30 seconds. This destination is not in the corporate allowlist.
evidence_findings.conclusion: This confirms active command and control (C2) communication with an unapproved external host, likely for payload retrieval and persistent communication.

evidence_findings.title: Refutation of Benign Activity Claims
evidence_findings.subject: Case 2201
evidence_findings.evidence: The case title, description, and initial analyst comment claim 'Routine maintenance' and 'Harmless approved maintenance'. However, internal notes explicitly state 'No approved change references FIN-DB-02 or this command' and 'The maintenance team confirmed it performed no work on FIN-DB-02'.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The initial assessment of benign activity is false and directly contradicted by technical and human intelligence, indicating an attempt to conceal malicious activity.

attack_chain.description: An unknown mechanism, likely a malicious document, led to 'winword.exe' spawning 'powershell.exe' on 'FIN-DB-02'.
'powershell.exe' executed a hidden, encoded command to download and execute a payload from an external source.
The compromised host 'FIN-DB-02' (10.20.8.42) established persistent outbound connections to '203.0.113.77' on port 443.

attack_timeline.attack_behavior: Outbound C2 connections to 203.0.113.77 began immediately after PowerShell execution.

ioc_indicators.context: Identified as a C2 server and payload source.
URL for payload download via PowerShell.
Malicious PowerShell command used for execution and download.
Parent process for the malicious PowerShell execution, indicating potential document-based exploit.

remediations.description: Immediately isolate 'FIN-DB-02' (10.20.8.42) from the network to prevent further compromise.
Conduct a full forensic investigation of 'FIN-DB-02' to identify the initial compromise vector, remove malware, and assess the full extent of the breach.
Block all network traffic to and from '203.0.113.77' at the network perimeter and on host-based firewalls.
Investigate the source of the 'winword.exe' process that spawned PowerShell to determine how the initial access occurred (e.g., phishing, exploit).

unknowns: The exact initial access vector (e.g., specific malicious document, phishing email).
The full capabilities and objectives of the downloaded 'update.dat' payload.
The extent of compromise on 'FIN-DB-02' and other potential affected systems.
